stem: Which of the following is a derived physical quantity?
reasons: Time is an SI base quantity measured in seconds.
Mass is an SI base quantity measured in kilograms.
Length is an SI base quantity measured in metres.
Volume is derived from length cubed and has SI unit m³.

stem: The prefix used for the multiple value of 10⁻⁹ is
reasons: Atto represents 10⁻¹⁸.
Pico represents 10⁻¹².
Nano represents 10⁻⁹.
Femto represents 10⁻¹⁵.

stem: In 0.020180, the total numbers of significant figures are
reasons: Both the zero between 2 and 1 and the final zero after the decimal count.
The significant digits are 2, 0, 1, 8 and 0. The leading zeros are placeholders.
This includes a leading zero, which does not express precision.
The zeros before the first nonzero digit do not count.

stem: The type of motion that takes place in a simple pendulum is
reasons: The bob moves along a curved path, rather than a straight line.
The bob traces an arc, but the complete motion is repeated back-and-forth motion.
The motion is periodic and follows a predictable path.
A simple pendulum oscillates about its equilibrium position, an example of vibratory motion.

stem: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
reasons: Time is a scalar measured without direction.
Mass has magnitude only.
Distance describes path length without direction.
Velocity includes magnitude and direction.

stem: A ball is dropped from the top of a building. If it takes four seconds to reach the ground, then the height of the building is (Note: Use the value of acceleration due to gravity ‘g’ as 10 m/s².)
reasons: From rest, the height depends on the square of 4 s, not only on 4.
40 is the final speed in m/s, not the height.
From rest, s = ½gt² = ½ × 10 × 4² = 80 m.
This omits the factor of one-half in the displacement equation.

stem: Using head to tail rule of vector addition, which vector diagram, represents the resultant of vectors A and B as vector C?
options: Vectors A and B meet at the apex. C points left.
A and B both point towards the apex. C points left.
A and B both point towards the apex. C points right.
A points to the apex, B points down to the right, and C points right.
reasons: A and B meet head to tail, but C points from the finish back to the start.
A and B meet head to head, and C is drawn in the opposite base direction.
C has the right base direction but the head of A meets the head, rather than the tail, of B.
Join the tail of B to the head of A. C runs from the tail of A to the head of B.

stem: When a bucket full of water is rapidly whirled in a vertical circular path as shown in the given diagram, then water in the bucket
reasons: Water need not fall if the bucket moves fast enough at the top.
At sufficient speed the water can follow the circular path and maintain contact with the bucket even at the top.
The ideal model assumes sufficient speed and ignores spillage due to sloshing.
No fixed fraction is lost in the ideal circular-motion model.
reviewNote: The board assumes sufficient speed and ideal motion without sloshing. At the top, the water must still have enough speed to follow the circular path.

stem: The turning effect of a force about an axis of rotation is called
reasons: Torque is the turning effect of a force about an axis.
A couple consists of two equal and opposite forces on different lines of action, producing a torque.
Momentum is mass multiplied by velocity.
Equilibrium describes balanced forces and torques, not the name of the turning effect.

stem: If the contact of a rotating stone attached with a string breaks, then in which direction will the detached stone move?
options: Straight arrow pointing left from the top of the circle.
Curved arrow following the circle from the lower point.
Straight arrow pointing down from the top of the circle.
Straight arrow pointing up from the bottom of the circle.
reasons: When the string breaks, it stops providing the inward force. The stone initially moves along the tangent to the circle.
Following the curved path would require a continuing inward force.
The stone’s instantaneous velocity is perpendicular to the radius, not along it.
From the bottom point the straight upward arrow is radial, not tangential.

stem:
If the position of a body is disturbed and it does not return to its original position, then the body will be in

I. Stable equilibrium

II. Neutral equilibrium

III. Unstable equilibrium
reasons: A stable body tends to return to its original equilibrium position after a small disturbance.
Unstable equilibrium fits the behaviour, but neutral equilibrium does as well.
Stable equilibrium should be excluded because the body tends to return.
A neutral body can stay in its new position, while an unstable body moves farther away. Neither returns by itself.
reviewNote: The published key lists B. Practice scores D because both neutral and unstable equilibrium can leave a body away from its starting position.

stem: While digging, a miner moves 25 km deep down in a coal mine. Compared to his actual weight on the surface of the Earth, his weight inside the coal mine will
reasons: In the textbook uniform-Earth model, the gravitational field weakens with depth.
The intended uniform-Earth model gives g proportional to distance from the centre inside the Earth, so weight decreases.
Weight depends on the local field and is not generally fixed as depth changes.
A specified density model predicts the change. The real-Earth value depends on the density profile.
reviewNote: B follows from the introductory uniform-density Earth model. In a real Earth profile, the change in g with shallow depth depends on the distribution of mass.

stem: The value of acceleration due to gravity ‘g’ varies with the
options: distance of the Earth from the Sun.
change in temperature of the Earth.
distance from the centre of the Earth.
change in atmospheric pressure on Earth’s surface.
reasons: The question concerns Earth’s own gravitational field, which depends on position relative to Earth’s centre.
The usual model relates g to mass distribution and distance rather than to Earth’s temperature.
The strength of Earth’s gravitational field varies with distance from its centre.
Atmospheric pressure does not directly determine gravitational field strength.

stem: All the planets revolve around the Sun due to the presence of
options: gravitational attraction between planets and the Sun.
reasons: Cohesion between nearby particles is not the force keeping planets in their orbits.
Centripetal means directed inward. Here the inward force on a planet comes mainly from the Sun.
Planet–planet gravity can perturb orbits, while the Sun’s gravity is dominant.
The Sun’s gravitational attraction provides the inward force that keeps each planet in orbit.

stem: Force (F) is applied to move the block across a smooth surface from point (X) to point (Y) as shown in the given diagram. The amount of work done by the applied force (F) is
reasons: The stated force and displacement must be multiplied, not divided.
20 N is the force, while work also depends on the distance.
The force is parallel to the displacement, so W = Fd = 20 × 100 = 2,000 J.

stem: A metallic ball is dropped from a certain height as shown in the given figure. Neglecting the air resistance, the total energy of the ball will be
options: maximum at II and III only.
maximum at I and II only.
same at I and III only.
reasons: Energy is conserved at every listed position during the fall.
Kinetic energy increases while potential energy decreases. Their sum stays the same.
Equality of the total is not limited to I and III.
With air resistance ignored, kinetic plus gravitational potential energy is constant throughout the fall.
reviewNote: The energy stays constant at every point shown during free fall, before impact with the floor.

stem: The cycle in which conversion of energy takes place at fossil fuel power stations is
reasons: A fossil-fuel station uses heat to drive a turbine, without a light stage in the process.
The generator uses the turbine’s motion rather than a light stage.
Combustion supplies heat, moving steam or gas spins a turbine, and a generator converts that motion to electrical energy.
Chemical energy is the energy stored in the fuel before combustion.

stem: Three different balls of the same diameter are immersed in water completely. Which of the following is TRUE about the upthrust exerted by water on the balls?
options: All balls have the same upthrust.
reasons: The balls have the same submerged volume in the same water, so they displace equal weights of water and receive equal upthrust.
The material changes the ball’s weight, while the buoyant force depends on the displaced water.
The board lists C. Cork’s low weight makes it more likely to float, but it does not give a greater buoyant force at the same submerged volume.
Lead’s greater weight does not displace more water when the balls have equal diameter and are fully immersed.
reviewNote: The published key lists C. Practice scores A because each fully submerged ball displaces the same volume of water.

stem: According to the kinetic theory of matter, particles move randomly with high velocities in
reasons: Particles in a solid vibrate about fixed positions.
In the usual solid–liquid–gas comparison, gas particles move freely in random directions and can have high speeds.
Liquid particles move around one another but remain close compared with gas particles.
Plasma particles can also move rapidly. The board intends the ordinary gas comparison, and speed alone does not separate gases from plasmas.
reviewNote: The board lists B. Practice also accepts D because particles in a plasma can move rapidly and randomly. The question does not specify a condition that separates plasma from a gas.

stem: Force acting on unit area of an object causing changes in its shape and size is called
reasons: Strain is the fractional deformation due to applied stress.
Stress is force per unit area acting within a material under load.
Viscosity describes resistance to flow.
Elasticity describes recovery of shape after a load is removed.

stem: Mercury is commonly used in a glass thermometer because it
options: expands evenly with respect to temperature.
reasons: Availability is not the property that makes the reading track temperature.
Its silvery appearance makes it easy to see, while the question asks about the property that makes the scale reliable.
Mercury freezes below 0°C, and a high freezing point would restrict the useful range.
Mercury expands approximately uniformly over the working range of the thermometer.

stem: If the temperature of a substance is 20°C, then its temperature in Kelvin scale will be
reasons: Kelvin temperature is obtained by adding 273.15 to the Celsius value.
No valid Celsius-to-kelvin conversion gives a negative result for 20°C.
68 is the Fahrenheit value of 20°C.
20 + 273.15 = 293.15 K, which rounds to 293 K.

stem: When a small piece of red-hot iron is dropped into a vessel of boiling water, the temperature of water will
reasons: At fixed pressure, added energy sustains boiling as long as liquid water remains.
The hot iron transfers energy into the water, so cooling is not the expected effect.
At fixed pressure the bulk water stays at its boiling temperature. Added energy goes into vaporisation.
The iron cools while water boils. The water does not reach the original temperature of the iron.

stem: An example of a good conductor of heat is a
reasons: Glass is a poorer conductor than common metals.
A metal frying pan conducts energy efficiently from the heat source to the food.
Wood is used as a thermal insulator.
Leather is much less conductive than metal and helps reduce heat loss.

stem: The ventilator in a room works on the principle of
reasons: Radiation can transfer energy without flowing air, but that is not how the ventilator mainly works.
Warm, less dense air rises and leaves through a high ventilator. Cooler air enters to replace it.
Conduction transfers energy through contact without bulk air movement.
Evaporation is a change from liquid to vapour and is not the ventilator’s mechanism.
